item.title: Retaining wall broken by motorists, 12th August
item.description:
I am writing to report further damage to the low brick wall on the traffic island at the junction of St George's Road and Westminster Bridge Road. Firstly, I would like to thank the Council for carrying out repairs to the wall approximately two months ago. The work was much appreciated. Unfortunately, shortly after the repairs were completed, the wall sustained further damage, almost certainly as a result of vehicles striking it. Given the location of the traffic island, this appears to be a recurring problem rather than an isolated incident. May I suggest that the Council considers installing a number of metal bollards along the edge of the traffic island to protect the low brick walls from further vehicle impacts? While there would be an initial cost, I believe this would reduce the need for repeated repairs and provide a more durable long-term solution. I would be grateful if the damage could be inspected and repaired once again, and if the possibility of installing protective bollards could be considered as part of the works.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 147, Westminster Bridge Road, Elephant and Castle, Greater London

item.title: Bench only used by homeless to drink, 12th August
item.description:
I am writing to request that Southwark Council considers removing the public bench on St George's Road, near the junction with Lambeth Road, directly in front of St George's Cathedral. Unfortunately, the bench is regularly used by homeless individuals and others who gather there for extended periods. We have no wish to stigmatise anyone, but the ongoing behaviour associated with the use of this bench has become a significant problem. There are frequent incidents of broken bottles, discarded food, litter and other rubbish being left around, on and underneath the seat. Much of this waste is thrown over the Cathedral railings onto our property, leaving us to clear it up on a daily basis. We have no control over the people using the bench, yet we are continually dealing with the consequences of their behaviour, which has a negative impact on the appearance, cleanliness and safety of the Cathedral grounds. Looking ahead, we are exploring the possibility of installing seating within our own forecourt, where it can be properly managed and maintained. In contrast, the existing public bench appears to serve little purpose other than as a gathering place where antisocial behaviour regularly occurs.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): St George's Road, Elephant and Castle, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
